display: Beekeeper and honey seller at two Austin farmers markets, with sixteen years of keeping bees.

signals.text: I may need somewhere to keep about forty beehives by spring, within 45 minutes of Austin.
The land my bees sit on is likely to be sold by the end of October, and I haven't told my customers yet.
I want to move the hives before November, because winter moves are risky for the colonies.
I'm looking for a yard with no pesticide spraying nearby and an owner who is fine with a small commercial beekeeper.
The drought has been hard on the bees. The wildflowers failed, so the colonies are light going into winter and I'm feeding syrup every week.
I'm replacing queens in about a dozen weak colonies this fall, and the new queens arrive by mail in early October.
I'm pouring about 400 beeswax candles for the holiday markets and could use a more efficient way to make them than muffin tins and a double boiler.
The land question weighs on me more than I let on. I'd welcome someone who just listens, without trying to fix it.
Money is tight right now. I'm putting off truck brake repairs so I can afford the new queens.
My knees are worn out, and I wonder how many more years I can lift heavy hive boxes.
My daughter wants me closer, and I haven't told her how uncertain the land situation is.

offers.text: Raw honey in three varieties (wildflower, mesquite, sumac), sold as 'Brannigan Bees' at the Sunset Valley and Mueller farmers markets, about 220 jars a month in season.
Sixteen years of Texas beekeeping experience, including requeening, drought feeding, hive moves and extraction, which I can teach or consult on.
Handmade beeswax candles and comb honey for the holidays, in bulk for churches, gift shops and corporate gifts.
Pollination for orchards, gardens and small farms, with colonies placed where there's no pesticide spraying.
An extraction shed with a four-frame extractor and a heated uncapping knife. I could extract a small beekeeper's honey, or lend a hand to someone starting out.
Regular Saturday and Sunday market stalls with loyal customers, where I could carry complementary local products or introduce a new maker.
A flatbed truck and experience moving hives safely at night.
A circle of about 60 church families who buy candles every Christmas, plus a choir community, reachable through me.
Bass voice and sixteen years in a gospel choir, plus a long-haul trucker's lifetime of road stories.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I own about ten acres east of Austin with wildflowers and no spraying. I'd love to host a few beehives, and I'd take honey as the rent.
catchers.can: I can move up to forty hives there before November and pay in honey and pollination. I can also teach the landowner what living beside bees is like.
catchers.confirm: Is the land within about 45 minutes of Austin, and free of pesticide spraying nearby?

catchers.hypo: I run a small orchard and my fruit set was poor this year. Do you rent hives for pollination in the spring?
catchers.can: I can place healthy colonies in the orchard for the bloom and advise on timing, hive density and pesticide-safe practices.
catchers.confirm: Do you avoid spraying insecticides during bloom?

catchers.hypo: I'm a small business owner and want 200 beeswax candles as holiday gifts for clients, ideally local and handmade.
catchers.can: I can supply handmade beeswax candles in bulk from November, with a label and small-batch customization.
catchers.confirm: Is your order for 30 or more candles, with delivery in Austin before mid-December?

catchers.hypo: I want to start with a couple of hives next spring. Can someone local show me what a beekeeper's year really looks like?
catchers.can: I can walk a newcomer through a hive inspection, the seasonal work and a honey harvest, and help them avoid the usual first-year mistakes.
catchers.confirm: Are you in the Austin area and willing to spend a few weekend mornings in a bee suit?

catchers.hypo: My church has an unused half-acre behind the fellowship hall. Would a beekeeper be interested in it?
catchers.can: I'd be glad to talk it over. A church yard where I know the people would be a good home, and I could repay it with honey, candles and bee-education events.
catchers.confirm: Would the congregation be comfortable with a few dozen hives on site, with a fenced or screened area and a nearby water source?

catchers.hypo: I'm a retired mechanic and I like fixing old trucks. Does anyone need brakes done cheaply on an older F-250?
catchers.can: A mechanic friend from my church choir could look at a truck's brakes, and I could help by trading honey or candles for the labor.
catchers.confirm: Is it an older full-size pickup, and would you accept a trade of honey or candles for part of the cost?

catchers.hypo: I'm losing the place I've worked for years because the owner is selling, and I don't know what to do next.
catchers.can: I know what it's like to lose a place your livelihood depends on. I can talk it through and share how I'm handling it.
catchers.confirm: Is it more that you want someone who has been through something similar to talk to, rather than a solution?

catchers.hypo: I run a farmers market or a holiday pop-up and need a local honey and candle vendor for the season.
catchers.can: I can take a holiday stall and bring candles, honey and comb. I'm already at two Austin markets and can add a third if the timing works.
catchers.confirm: Is the market in the Austin area, and can I get a stall by November?

forbids.text: I won't place bees where there is pesticide spraying.
My hives have to stay within 45 minutes of Austin so I can keep both markets.
I can't pay commercial land rental rates.
I avoid moving colonies in winter, so land moves need to happen before November.
I don't share exact hive locations with strangers.
I won't sell diluted or blended honey under my label.

projects.name: New home for the hives
projects.text: Find a safe, spray-free yard within 45 minutes of Austin for about forty Langstroth hives before November, ideally with an owner who values pollination and honey.

projects.name: Christmas candle batch
projects.text: Pour about 400 beeswax candles for the holiday markets and church orders, and find a faster, safer way to make them.

policy.t1: Hive count, what kind of land I need and when, the timing of the land situation, and the church and market connections.
policy.t2: Finances, health limits, family worries, and which friends could help with the move or repairs.
policy.never: Bank details and the exact locations of my hives.
